previous_statement: Dependency bridge and defect estimate. Require nodes 1.2 and 1.3.1 to be validated. Thus, uniformly in n, gamma_n has involution and multiplicative defects at most K_hom e and satisfies c_0 <= a_n <= b_n <= 5. For X, insert gamma_n(X^dagger)gamma_n(X) between gamma_n(X^dagger X) and gamma_n(X)^dagger gamma_n(X). The target product-norm axiom yields an error at most K_hom e[1+(1+epsilon)b_n]||X||^2. Under e<=1 (so epsilon<=1) and b_n<=5 this is at most D e||X||^2 with the universal choice D=11K_hom.
new_statement: Dependency bridge and defect estimate in the common small-defect regime. Require validated nodes 1.2 and 1.3.1, and put e_bridge:=min{1,e_hom,e_mod}, where e_hom is the universal threshold in node 1.2 and e_mod is the universal threshold supplied by the validated proof of node 1.3.1. Assume e:=rho+epsilon<e_bridge. Then node 1.2 applies (since e<e_hom) and, uniformly in n, gamma_n has involution and multiplicative defects at most K_hom e; node 1.3.1 applies (since e<e_mod) and gives c_0<=a_n<=b_n<=5. For X, insert gamma_n(X^dagger)gamma_n(X) between gamma_n(X^dagger X) and gamma_n(X)^dagger gamma_n(X). The multiplicative defect contributes at most K_hom e||X||^2. For the other difference, the target product-norm axiom and the involution defect give ||[gamma_n(X^dagger)-gamma_n(X)^dagger]gamma_n(X)||<=(1+epsilon)K_hom e||X||||gamma_n(X)||<=(1+epsilon)b_n K_hom e||X||^2. Hence the total error is at most K_hom e[1+(1+epsilon)b_n]||X||^2. Because e<e_bridge<=1, epsilon<=e<1, and b_n<=5, the bracket is at most 11. Thus the error is at most D e||X||^2 with the universal choice D=11K_hom.
